title: How we work | Alai Labs
description: How Alai Labs builds and deploys edge AI: from defining the problem to a model on site, sizing edge servers, industrial IoT, and remote operation through digital twins.

head.p_1: We build AI that runs at the edge, on hardware sized for the site, connected to the sensors and machines already there, and watched remotely. Here is how a deployment comes together.

build.p_1: Every model starts from one operational problem, not from a technique. We work through it in the same order each time, so you can see where a project stands.
build.li_1: Define the problem. Agree what the model must detect, measure or decide, and what counts as good enough on site.
build.li_2: Prepare the data. Collect and clean images or sensor readings from the real environment.
build.li_3: Choose the model. Pick an approach that fits the job and the hardware it will run on.
build.li_5: Evaluate it against the targets agreed in step one.
build.li_6: Tune it until it meets those targets on site conditions.
build.li_7: Deploy it to the edge device on site.

sizing.p_1: Running models on site means results do not wait on a link to the cloud. That only works if the hardware is sized for the real load and the real environment. We size each industrial edge server in five checks.
sizing.li_1: Workload. How many models, cameras and sensors, and how often each must run.
sizing.li_2: Compute and storage. The processors, accelerators and storage that workload needs.
sizing.li_3: Network and latency. How fast results must arrive, and what links the site has.
sizing.li_4: Power and thermal. What the site can supply and how hot or exposed the device will be.
sizing.li_5: Test. Run the full workload on the chosen hardware before it goes live.

iiot.p_1: Sensors give the models something to work with and show where assets are. We use outdoor-rated hardware and keep the network secure from sensor to dashboard.
iiot.li_2: UWB, BLE and active tags for location and occupancy

remote.p_1: Robots and sensors are linked to a 3D digital twin of the site, so your team can see what is happening and take control remotely.
remote.li_1: 3D digital twin for remote control and monitoring
remote.li_2: Digital twins and augmented reality for manufacturing

security.p_1: How data is stored and protected, who supports a deployment and from where, and typical project timelines. To be supplied by the Alai team.
